<!-- pr-reviewer: e7d49a2a5070c6bb464f695ca14460d59f466d51 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

**What looks good**
- Safety check, as asked: a grouped Weldon pick is only a lookup. `resolve`/`weldon_for` (`crates/tools/src/holder_library_weldon.rs:60-90`) return an existing per-bore `HolderEntry` unchanged, so outline, body diameter and collision bands are the per-bore entry's own. `a_picked_weldon_draws_the_old_entrys_collision_bands` compares the bands band for band for every bore of every taper.
- An unfit shank is refused, never mapped to the nearest bore. Fit uses the existing `fits_shank` (`BORE_SLACK` 0.02 mm, so no two bores overlap and the match is unambiguous). A miss, or a NaN shank, returns `LibraryError::Shank` naming the taper's bores. `library_body` (`commands/tool_body.rs:79`) still runs `fits_shank` on the resolved entry, and `AddTool` fails at that call before its `unwrap_or(entry)` fallback is reached. The refusal is also pinned through the command in `crates/app/tests/holder_library.rs`.
- The data is unchanged. Every Weldon taper uses one gauge length for all its bores, so the UI default gauge taken from the first bore matches the resolved entry.
- No unwrap/expect outside tests. The new code is in `camcraft-tools` (lowest crate), with a provenance line, files under 400 lines, and a decision file (`docs/decisions/2018-weldon-per-taper.md`). No new crate dependency, no process files, no snapshot PNGs, no CHANGELOG edit.

**Results merged with main (locally on macOS, not the runner; clean trial merge with upstream/main)**
| step | result |
|---|---|
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` (tools lib, 20 app suites, 14 ui suites) | all green, 1522 passed, 0 failed, 8 ignored |
| 4 new `holder_library::weldon::tests` + `the_picker_lists...` | pass |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

No `cfg(windows)` or per-OS values are touched, so no Windows run is owed.

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- A machine `.mch` `tooling.default_holder` still takes only a per-bore name, as the PR says. #2016 will need the tool's shank at mount time to take a grouped default.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
